conditions.name: Congenital hypothyroidism

sources.title: Newborn Screening Guidelines for Congenital Hypothyroidism in India: Recommendations of the Indian Society for Pediatric and Adolescent Endocrinology (ISPAE) - Part II: Imaging, Treatment and Follow-up (Sudhanshu S, et al. Indian J Pediatr 2018;85:448-453). Only the abstract and summary were readable; the full text is behind a paywall.

Newborn Screening Guidelines for Congenital Hypothyroidism in India: ISPAE Recommendations - Part I: Screening and Confirmation of Diagnosis (Desai MP, et al. Indian J Pediatr 2018;85:440-447). Abstract only.
IAP Standard Treatment Guidelines 2022: Hypothyroidism (Ayyavoo A, Kumar R, Godbole T)

Congenital Hypothyroidism: A 2020-2021 Consensus Guidelines Update - An ENDO-European Reference Network Initiative Endorsed by ESPE and ESE (van Trotsenburg P, et al. Thyroid 2021;31:387-419). Read through the Europe PMC full-text copy of PMC8001676.
Thyroxine: brands and prices in India (used only for tablet strengths)

investigation_sets.name: Confirm diagnosis
investigation_sets.when: Venous sample after a positive newborn screen, before starting levothyroxine

items.note: ISPAE: primary CH and treatment if venous TSH >20 mIU/L before age 2 weeks, or >10 mIU/L after age 2 weeks.
ISPAE: low FT4 is <1.17 ng/dL. ENDO-ERN: start treatment if TSH >20 mU/L even when FT4 is normal.
Alternative to Free T4 where FT4 is not available. ISPAE: low T4 is <10 µg/dL.

investigation_sets.name: Find the cause (do not delay treatment)
investigation_sets.when: After CH is biochemically confirmed; start levothyroxine first, do not wait for scans

items.note: ISPAE and IAP: ultrasound and scintigraphy after biochemical confirmation.
IAP: scintigraphy can be done up to 7 days after starting levothyroxine (if TSH is high).
ENDO-ERN mentions serum thyroglobulin as useful in working out the cause. Optional.
ENDO-ERN: knee X-ray may be performed to assess the severity of intrauterine hypothyroidism. Optional.
ENDO-ERN and IAP: not just the neonatal test; repeat hearing tests before school age and as required.

investigation_sets.name: Follow-up on levothyroxine
investigation_sets.when: ISPAE schedule: T4/FT4 at 2 weeks; TSH and T4/FT4 at 1 month; then every 2 months till 6 months; every 3 months from 6 months to 3 years; every 3-6 months thereafter

items.note: IAP: T4/FT4 should reach the upper half of the reference range by 2 weeks. ENDO-ERN: take blood before, or at least 4 hours after, the day's levothyroxine.
IAP: TSH should reach the lower half of the reference range by 4 weeks. ENDO-ERN: keep TSH within the reference interval; extra check 4-6 weeks after any change of dose or formulation.

investigation_sets.name: Re-evaluation at 3 years
investigation_sets.when: Children with possible transient CH (for example a normally placed gland, no firm diagnosis of permanent CH): at age 3 years, after stopping levothyroxine

items.note: IAP: treatment can be stopped for 4 weeks at 3 years of age. ENDO-ERN: phase out over 4-6 weeks or just stop, then retest; TSH >=10 mU/L confirms primary hypothyroidism.
Measured with TSH at re-evaluation.

medicines.dose_guide: 10-15 mcg/kg in the neonatal period (ISPAE 2018); IAP 2022 writes this as 10-15 mcg/kg/day. Later doses are adjusted to TSH and T4/FT4; no age-wise maintenance dose table could be read from an Indian guideline.
medicines.duration: Continue; re-evaluate at age 3 years if transient CH is possible
medicines.instructions: Give once a day at the same time every day. Crush the tablet and give it in a little water or breast milk with a spoon. Avoid giving with soy protein or high-fibre feeds.
medicines.monitoring: T4/FT4 at 2 weeks; TSH and T4/FT4 at 1 month, then every 2 months till 6 months, every 3 months from 6 months to 3 years, and every 3-6 months thereafter (ISPAE). Recheck 4-6 weeks after a dose change (ENDO-ERN).
medicines.indication: Primary congenital hypothyroidism, started as soon as the venous confirmatory sample is taken and the result supports CH; IAP: as soon as possible and no later than the first 2 weeks of life.
medicines.quote: Levothyroxine is commenced at 10-15 μg/kg in the neonatal period.
medicines.note: ISPAE abstract gives the dose per kg without '/day'; IAP STG 2022 states 'Initial thyroxine dose is 10-15 μg/kg/day'. ENDO-ERN 2020-21 differs slightly: starting dose 'up to 15 μg/kg per day', highest dose (10-15) for severe CH, about 10 for mild, and 5-10 may be considered for the mildest forms. Administration advice (same time daily, crushed tablet in water or breast milk, avoid soy and vegetable fibre, may be given with food) is from ENDO-ERN, because the ISPAE full text could not be opened. ENDO-ERN did not mention iron or calcium, so no spacing rule for those is given here. Strengths are from an Indian drug index (which also lists 37 mcg and 200 mcg), not from a formulary.

rx.name: Levothyroxine tablet
rx.instructions: Give once a day at the same time every day. Crush the tablet and give it in a little water or breast milk with a spoon. Avoid giving with soy protein or high-fibre feeds.

advice.text: Give the thyroid tablet every day at the same time. Do not stop it without asking the doctor.
Crush the tablet and give it in a spoon with a little water or breast milk.
Avoid soy-based feeds close to the dose.
Come for blood tests on the dates given. On the day of the test, give the tablet after the blood sample or at least 4 hours before it.
Hearing should be checked again before school age.

conditions.caveats: 1) The ISPAE 2018 Part I and Part II full texts are paywalled; only the abstracts were read. The confirmatory thresholds, starting dose, follow-up schedule and 3-year re-evaluation are from those abstracts; target ranges and the follow-up intervals in IAP STG 2022 (which broadly repeats ISPAE) were read from the IAP PDF. 2) Follow-up intervals differ: ISPAE 2-monthly to 6 months then 3-monthly to 3 years; IAP STG '1-2 monthly until 6 months and 2-4 monthly from 6 to 36 months'; ENDO-ERN first review 1-2 weeks after starting, then every 2 weeks until TSH is normal, every 1-3 months to 12 months, every 2-4 months from 1 to 3 years, every 3-6 months until growth is complete. 3) ENDO-ERN says a child with a gland in situ who needs less than 3 mcg/kg per day at 6 months can be re-evaluated then. 4) ENDO-ERN recommends a careful examination of every neonate with high TSH for malformations, particularly cardiac (no routine echocardiogram is stated). 5) Central congenital hypothyroidism is not given its own entry: ENDO-ERN says to start levothyroxine only after adrenal function is shown to be intact, and to keep FT4 above the middle of the reference range. 6) ENDO-ERN advises against compounded levothyroxine solutions or suspensions. 7) Quotes were extracted through a web-fetch tool and should be spot-checked against the papers.

conditions.name: Acquired hypothyroidism

sources.title: IAP Standard Treatment Guidelines 2022: Hypothyroidism (Ayyavoo A, Kumar R, Godbole T)
2014 European Thyroid Association Guidelines for the Management of Subclinical Hypothyroidism in Pregnancy and in Children (Lazarus J, et al. Eur Thyroid J 2014;3:76-94)

Guidelines for the Treatment of Hypothyroidism, American Thyroid Association Task Force on Thyroid Hormone Replacement (Jonklaas J, et al. Thyroid 2014). Only the general (adult) sections on how to take levothyroxine could be read; the section on infants and children could not.
Subclinical Hypothyroidism in Children (Shriraam M, Sridhar M. Indian Pediatr 2014;51:889-895)
Thyroxine: brands and prices in India (used only for tablet strengths)

items.note: IAP: essential.
IAP: essential (total T4 or free T4).
Alternative to Free T4.
IAP: optional. ETA 2014 uses TPO antibody status to set how often to recheck subclinical hypothyroidism.
IAP: optional.
IAP: ultrasound if necessary, for primary hypothyroidism.
Only for central hypothyroidism (low FT4 without a raised TSH). IAP words this as 'MRI brain'.

investigation_sets.name: Follow-up on levothyroxine
investigation_sets.when: 4-6 weeks after starting or changing the dose; the IAP guideline gives no routine interval once the dose is stable

items.note: IAP: adjust the dose to keep TSH and T4/FT4 in range. The 4-6 week recheck after a dose change is from the ATA 2014 guideline (adult section).
With TSH.

investigation_sets.name: Subclinical hypothyroidism: watch without treatment
investigation_sets.when: Raised TSH with normal T4/FT4, child over 3 years, not on levothyroxine. Antibodies negative: recheck at 1 year, then less often if no worsening. Antibodies positive: every 6-12 months; more often if the first TSH was above 10 mU/L.

items.note: ETA 2014 recommendations 26 and 28. Confirm a raised TSH on a repeat sample before labelling (Indian Pediatrics review).
Must be normal for the label 'subclinical'.
ETA 2014: monitor TSH and TPO antibody in antibody-negative children; TSH with or without TPO antibody in antibody-positive children.

medicines.dose_guide: By weight: age 1-3 years 4-6 mcg/kg; age 3-10 years 3-5 mcg/kg; age 10-16 years 2-4 mcg/kg. Or by body surface area: 100 mcg/m². Long-standing, severe, untreated hypothyroidism: start at a lower dose and step up over several weeks. (IAP STG 2022)
medicines.instructions: Take once a day, consistently either 60 minutes before breakfast or at bedtime. Keep it apart from iron, calcium and other medicines that interfere with absorption.
medicines.monitoring: TSH and T4/FT4; adjust the dose to keep both in range (IAP). Recheck TSH 4-6 weeks after any dose change (ATA 2014).
medicines.indication: Overt acquired primary hypothyroidism (for example Hashimoto thyroiditis). In subclinical hypothyroidism (raised TSH, normal FT4) the decision to treat is individual: ETA 2014 finds insufficient evidence to treat most children with TSH below 10 mU/L.
medicines.quote: Age 1-3 years: 4-6 µg/kg body weight; Age 3-10 years: 3-5 µg/kg; Age 10-16 years: 2-4 µg/kg; 100 µg/m2 BSA (OR)
medicines.note: The IAP table gives doses per kg body weight without writing '/day'; they are daily doses. It gives no band under 1 year (use the congenital hypothyroidism entry) or over 16 years. The quote joins four separate lines of the IAP table. The timing advice (60 minutes before breakfast or at bedtime; separate from interfering medicines) is from the ATA 2014 guideline's general recommendations 3a and 3b, which were written for adults; that guideline calls a 4-hour separation 'traditional, but untested'. The IAP guideline says nothing on how to take the tablet. Strengths are from an Indian drug index.

rx.name: Levothyroxine tablet
rx.instructions: Take once a day, consistently either 60 minutes before breakfast or at bedtime. Keep it apart from iron, calcium and other medicines that interfere with absorption.

advice.text: Take the thyroid tablet every day at the same time, either 60 minutes before breakfast or at bedtime.
Keep iron and calcium medicines well apart from the thyroid tablet.
Do not stop the tablet on your own; the treatment is usually long term.
A blood test is needed 4-6 weeks after any change of dose.

conditions.caveats: 1) No Indian guideline was found that gives a follow-up interval for a child on a stable levothyroxine dose, a TSH target, or a treatment threshold for subclinical hypothyroidism; the IAP STG 2022 is silent on all three. 2) Subclinical hypothyroidism guidance is from ETA 2014: under 3 years with TSH not normalised after 1 month of age, treat until 3 years then trial off; over 3 years, monitor as set out above; treatment decision after discussion with parents; 'reasonable to treat' after thyroid irradiation; regular thyroid monitoring in trisomy 21. ETA 2014 gives no levothyroxine dose for children. 3) ETA 2014 notes that a TSH of 5-7 mU/L in an obese child is likely the consequence, not the cause, of the obesity. 4) The Indian Pediatrics 2014 article is a review, not a guideline; it is used only for 'repeat the TSH before labelling' and agrees that treatment is not justified when TSH is below 10 mIU/L without other risk factors. 5) The paediatric section of the ATA 2014 hypothyroidism guideline and the BNF for Children could not be opened, so their age-wise doses are not included. 6) Screening for coeliac disease or type 1 diabetes in autoimmune thyroiditis is not included: no guideline statement was found for it from the thyroid side. 7) Quotes were extracted through a web-fetch tool and should be spot-checked.

conditions.name: Graves disease / hyperthyroidism

sources.title: IAP Standard Treatment Guidelines 2022: Hyperthyroidism (Riaz I, Bhakhri BK, Mehta S). Read only through a Medical Dialogues summary dated 16 April 2023; the IAP PDF itself could not be opened.
2022 European Thyroid Association Guideline for the management of pediatric Graves' disease (Mooij CF, et al. Eur Thyroid J 2022;11(1):e210073). Read from the copy hosted by BSPED.
Carbimazole, propranolol and atenolol: brands and prices in India (used only for strengths)
Medical management of children with thyrotoxicosis: treatment (regional guideline; used only as a cross-check)

items.note: Suppressed in hyperthyroidism.
ETA: recommended for all paediatric patients with hyperthyroidism; if negative but Graves disease is likely, repeat after a few weeks.
ETA: measure with TRAb.
ETA: ultrasound with Doppler is preferred to scintigraphy, to avoid radiation.
Not routine. ETA: better for identifying a 'hot' autonomous nodule. IAP: shows increased uptake in Graves disease.
Baseline, with neutrophil count, before the first dose (IAP and ETA).
Baseline, before the first dose (IAP and ETA).

investigation_sets.name: Follow-up on antithyroid drug
investigation_sets.when: IAP: free T4 and T3 every 4-6 weeks while titrating, then 3-monthly once euthyroid. ETA: every 4 weeks for the first 3 months, then 2-monthly and then 3-monthly depending on the course.

items.note: ETA: be guided by thyroid hormone levels, not TSH, in the first 4-6 months.
May stay suppressed for several months after FT4/FT3 are normal (ETA).

investigation_sets.name: Fever or sore throat on antithyroid drug
investigation_sets.when: Same day: stop the drug and test

items.note: With neutrophil count. ETA: stop the drug if neutrophils are below 0.5 x10^9/L; 0.5-1.5 can be watched with once or twice weekly counts.

investigation_sets.name: Signs of liver dysfunction on antithyroid drug (for example jaundice)
investigation_sets.when: When signs of liver dysfunction appear

items.note: ETA: transaminases more than three times the upper limit of normal warrant stopping the drug.

investigation_sets.name: Before stopping antithyroid drug
investigation_sets.when: After at least 3 years of treatment (ETA)

items.note: ETA: stop only when TRAb has been low for several months; if raised, remission is unlikely and the drug should not be stopped.

investigation_sets.name: After stopping antithyroid drug
investigation_sets.when: Every 3-4 months in the first year, every 6 months in the second year, then yearly (ETA)

items.note: Watching for relapse.

medicines.dose_guide: IAP STG 2022: 0.5-0.7 mg/kg/day. ETA 2022: initial 0.25-0.75 mg/kg daily; dose titration preferred, starting 0.25-0.5 mg/kg/day (up to 0.75 mg/kg/day in severe cases), then reduce by 25-50% as thyroid function normalises.
medicines.max: No mg ceiling is stated by IAP or ETA. ETA: if still thyrotoxic at about 1.3 mg/kg/day, discuss surgery or radioiodine.
medicines.duration: ETA: at least 3 years; consider 5 years or more if remission is unlikely. IAP: can be continued for 1-2 years if remission is not achieved, then consider definitive therapy.
medicines.instructions: Take once a day. STOP the tablet and get a blood count the same day if there is fever or sore throat. Report jaundice or a rash.
medicines.monitoring: Blood count with neutrophils and liver function before starting. Free T4 and T3 every 4-6 weeks while titrating, then 3-monthly (IAP). Blood count at once for fever or sore throat; liver tests if signs of liver dysfunction (ETA).
medicines.indication: First-line antithyroid drug for Graves disease in children (carbimazole or methimazole; not propylthiouracil).
medicines.quote: The initial antithyroid drug (ATD) dose is between 0.15 and 0.5 mg/kg of MMI or between 0.25 and 0.75 mg/kg of CBZ daily.
medicines.note: The quote is from ETA 2022, which was read directly. The IAP figure (0.5-0.7 mg/kg/day) is from a Medical Dialogues summary of the IAP guideline; it sits inside the ETA range. Neither says to divide the dose; ETA says once daily is sufficient. Block-and-replace (ETA: carbimazole 0.5-0.75 mg/kg/day with levothyroxine added in a low, age- and weight-appropriate dose once FT4/FT3 normalise) is described by ETA as having more adverse events in one trial; dose titration is preferred. A Scottish regional guideline caps the initial dose at 40 mg per day; this is not in IAP or ETA. Strengths are from an Indian drug index.

rx.name: Carbimazole tablet
rx.instructions: Take once a day. STOP the tablet and get a blood count the same day if there is fever or sore throat. Report jaundice or a rash.

medicines.dose_guide: IAP STG 2022: 0.1-1 mg/kg/day. ETA 2022: initial 0.15-0.5 mg/kg daily; dose titration preferred, starting 0.15-0.3 mg/kg/day (up to 0.5 mg/kg/day in severe cases), then reduce by 25-50% as thyroid function normalises.
medicines.max: No mg ceiling is stated by IAP or ETA. ETA: if still thyrotoxic at about 1.0 mg/kg/day, discuss surgery or radioiodine.
medicines.duration: ETA: at least 3 years; consider 5 years or more if remission is unlikely. IAP: can be continued for 1-2 years if remission is not achieved, then consider definitive therapy.
medicines.instructions: Take once a day. STOP the tablet and get a blood count the same day if there is fever or sore throat. Report jaundice or a rash.
medicines.indication: Alternative to carbimazole as first-line antithyroid drug for Graves disease in children.
medicines.quote: Methimazole (MMI) 0.1–1 mg/kg/d or carbimazole 0.5–0.7 mg/kg/d is preferred over propylthiouracil (PTU) among children.
medicines.note: The quote is the IAP STG 2022 wording as reproduced in a Medical Dialogues summary; the IAP PDF itself could not be opened. The IAP range (0.1-1 mg/kg/day) is wider than ETA 2022 (0.15-0.5 mg/kg/day initial; about 1.0 mg/kg/day is the point at which ETA says to discuss definitive treatment). No Indian drug-index listing for methimazole could be opened, so strengths are left blank. Carbimazole is converted to methimazole in the body; the two are not dose-for-dose equal (ETA gives separate ranges).

rx.name: Methimazole (thiamazole) tablet
rx.instructions: Take once a day. STOP the tablet and get a blood count the same day if there is fever or sore throat. Report jaundice or a rash.

medicines.dose_guide: IAP STG 2022: 1-2 mg/kg/day, titrated to symptoms. How the daily dose is divided is not stated in the summary that was read.
medicines.duration: Until thyroid hormone levels are controlled (ETA: stop once euthyroid)
medicines.instructions: For palpitations and tremor while the main medicine starts to work. Do not use in a child with asthma.
medicines.indication: Symptom control (tachycardia, tremor) in marked thyroid hormone excess, added to the antithyroid drug.
medicines.quote: Addition of beta-blockers like propranolol, 1–2 mg/kg/d helps in early control of symptoms
medicines.note: Marked not verified because the dose comes only from a Medical Dialogues summary of the IAP guideline (the IAP PDF could not be opened) and the number of doses per day is not given. ETA 2022 gives no figure: 'A beta-blocker (e.g. propranolol or atenolol) should be administered in an age- or weight-appropriate dose', avoided in asthma. As a cross-check, a Scottish regional guideline writes '250–750 µg/kg/dose three times per day'. BNF for Children could not be opened. Strengths are from an Indian drug index, which also lists sustained-release forms.

rx.name: Propranolol tablet
rx.instructions: For palpitations and tremor while the main medicine starts to work.

medicines.prescriber_note: Do not use in a child with asthma.

medicines.duration: Until thyroid hormone levels are controlled (ETA: stop once euthyroid)
medicines.indication: Alternative beta-blocker for symptom control, named by ETA 2022.
medicines.quote: A beta-blocker (e.g. propranolol or atenolol) should be administered in an age- or weight-appropriate dose.
medicines.note: The guideline names atenolol but gives no dose, and no other source with a paediatric thyrotoxicosis dose could be opened. Dose left blank for the doctor to fill in. Strengths are from an Indian drug index (which also lists 5 mg).

advice.text: If your child has fever or a sore throat: STOP the thyroid tablet and get a blood count done the same day.
Report jaundice (yellow eyes), a skin rash, blisters in the mouth or joint pains.
Treatment usually continues for several years. Do not stop the tablets without advice, even when your child feels well.
Blood tests are needed every 4-6 weeks at first, then every 3 months.

conditions.caveats: 1) PROPYLTHIOURACIL: ETA 2022 states 'Propylthiouracil (PTU) should not be used because of the risk of hepatic failure'; IAP prefers methimazole or carbimazole over PTU in children. PTU is deliberately not offered as a starter medicine. 2) Blood counts and liver tests: both IAP and ETA ask for them at baseline. ETA does not set a routine schedule during treatment; it asks for a neutrophil count with fever or sore throat and liver tests with signs of liver dysfunction. Stop the drug for neutrophils below 0.5 x10^9/L or transaminases above three times the upper limit of normal. 3) Duration differs: IAP 1-2 years before considering definitive therapy; ETA at least 3 years, and only stop when TRAb has been low for several months. 4) The IAP Standard Treatment Guideline on hyperthyroidism was read only through a Medical Dialogues summary; every IAP figure here should be checked against the IAP PDF. 5) The paediatric section of the ATA 2016 hyperthyroidism guideline could not be opened in any copy (every copy was cut off before that section), so its age-banded methimazole doses are not included. 6) Definitive treatment (ETA): radioiodine avoided under 5 years and used at 5-10 years only when surgery is not a realistic option; total thyroidectomy by a high-volume thyroid surgeon. IAP: surgery or radioiodine preferred for a toxic nodule or multinodular goitre. 7) Neonatal thyrotoxicosis is not covered by either source read. 8) Eye signs: ETA advises referral to an orbital specialist. 9) Quotes were extracted through a web-fetch tool and should be spot-checked.
